data.name: Talia
data.gender_notes: Talia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew talya, which means 'dew from God' or 'given by God'. In the Bible, the name Talia is not directly mentioned, but it is reminiscent of the biblical Talitha cum, meaning 'little girl, arise'. The name Talia carries the meaning “Dew of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Talia usually hope their child will grow to embody dew of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolic of new life and revival.
data.etymology: Talia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Dew of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Talia total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: טליה
in_hebrew.meaning: טליה היא שושנת השחר, טל הבוקר
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טליה הוא שם עברי שפירושו טל הבוקר, שושנת השחר. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'טל' שפירושו טל, ו'יה' שפירושו אלוהים. השם טליה מופיע בתנ"ך כמטפור עבור האלוהים המשפיע על עולמו, מביא טל ומשפיע על החיים. השם גם מתקשר לשושנת השחר, סמל לתקווה וחדשנות.

in_greek.name: Ταλιά
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ταλιά είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος טליה, που σημαίνει 'δροσιά' ή 'πρωινή δροσιά'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα Ταλιά, αλλά η έννοια της δροσιάς και της πρωινής ανανέωσης έχει πνευματική σημασία στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας. Το όνομα Ταλιά έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί στην Ελλάδα και σε άλλες ορθόδοξες κοινότητες ως σύμβολο ελπίδας και πνευματικής ανανέωσης.

in_latin.name: Talia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Talia derivatur ex hebraico טליה, quod significat 'ros' vel 'ros matutinus'. In primitiva Ecclesia Christiana, nomen Talia non invenitur directe, sed conceptus ros et renovationis matutinae habet significationem spiritualem. Nomen Talia usitatum est in traditione Christiana, praesertim in contextu devotionis ad Deum, qui vitam et spem afferre dignoscitur.

in_english.name: Talia
in_english.meaning: Talia means morning dew, symbolizing hope and renewal
in_english.long_meaning: The name Talia originates from the Hebrew name טליה (Talyah), meaning 'morning dew' or 'dew from God'. It symbolizes spiritual refreshment, hope, and renewal. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the concept of dew is significant, representing God's blessings and life-giving power (Psalm 130:6, Song of Solomon 5:14). In Christian tradition, Talia is associated with virtues of purity, innocence, and spiritual awakening. The name has been adopted across various Christian cultures, reflecting its universal themes of divine grace and new beginnings.

data.cultural_impact: The name Talia is appealing to individuals who value uniqueness and spiritual meaning in their personal identification. data.spiritual_significance: The name Talia is rooted in both the Biblical and Hebrew traditions, evoking a sense of divine favor and blessing. It serves as a powerful reminder that everything in life, including our names, is a gift from God. By choosing the name Talia, one embraces the spiritual belief that their existence and identity are graciously bestowed upon them by the divine creator. This name imparts a sense of gratitude and reverence, inspiring those who bear it to live their lives in accordance with God's will and enriching their connection to the divine through the very essence of their name.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Talia, meaning "little one" or "gentle flow" in Hebrew, symbolizes the nurturing and tender love of the divine mother, guiding and protecting her child on their spiritual journey.

historical_references.reference: In medieval legend, Talia was a nymph who was transformed into a willow tree by Mercury when he discovered her making love to another man while he was asleep. This story is depicted in several works of art, including a painting by Sandro Botticelli, 'The Story of Mercury and Talia'. This event is said to have occurred in ancient Italy.

Talia was also the name of a 16th-century Spanish noblewoman who was known for her exceptional beauty and grace. She was the wife of Don Fadrique Mendoza, the Duke of Calabria, and was celebrated in poetry and song by writers such as Miguel de Cervantes and Lope de Vega. This Talia lived during the Spanish Renaissance in the late 1500s.
